defect_class: A fix for a finding that describes a class of defect repairs, or adds a check against, only the instances the finding cites, so unnamed instances of the same class survive the fix.
why_picked: 1. Defect class: a finding describes a kind of defect and cites some sites as examples; the fixer repairs those sites and writes a check that lists them, so every unnamed instance of the class survives. 2. No current rule covers it: implementer-brief.md's FIX DISPATCH paragraph (quoted as `before`) tells the fixer to "fix exactly what that line names ... at its root cause", which a fixer reads as the cited sites; no paragraph of implementer-brief.md, implement.md, sdd-dispatch.md or engineering-principles.md says a class finding reaches its uncited instances. 3. It generalises: in one run, three consecutive fix rounds by two fixer kinds repeated it on one class (a gated fix renamed only the sampled ids, a panel fix added a denylist of exactly the reviewers' named ids and drew the class back as a new Important, and the next fix kept a denylist for multi-word ids that still passes about twenty such ids); the same shape applies to any finding about a naming rule, an unchecked error pattern, a missing guard clause or an unsafe call repeated across sites, in any language or layer. 4. It is a principle, not a patch: "a class finding is fixed for its class, and its check detects the class by shape, not by a list" names no id, file or tool.
before:
> **FIX DISPATCH:** a prompt carrying a `FIX INPUT:` line makes you a fixer, not a task's
> implementer: fix exactly what that line names — reviewer reports and finding refs, a
> `flow-guard close-task` refusal's lines, a wave member's commits to re-apply, or a failing suite block —
> at its root cause, under every other paragraph of this brief save the commit subject and trailer
> FLOW — COMMIT-PER-TASK names, which this paragraph's take the place of.
after:
> **FIX DISPATCH:** a prompt carrying a `FIX INPUT:` line makes you a fixer, not a task's
> implementer: fix exactly what that line names — reviewer reports and finding refs, a
> `flow-guard close-task` refusal's lines, a wave member's commits to re-apply, or a failing suite block —
> at its root cause, under every other paragraph of this brief save the commit subject and trailer
> FLOW — COMMIT-PER-TASK names, which this paragraph's take the place of. A finding that names a
> defect class — its note describing a kind of defect, or citing sites as examples — is fixed for
> every instance of that class in the code it reviewed, not only the sites it cites, and any check
> the fix adds detects the class by its shape, never by a list of the cited instances; before you
> report, search that code for the class once more and fix what the search finds.
